chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah and al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When the one who performs Dhihar divorces [his wife], then remarries her, upon him is the expiation."
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for Dhihar if the husband divorces and remarries his wife?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies a specific juristic nuance regarding *Dhihar*, establishing that remarriage to the same wife serves as the expiation (*kaffarah*) when the husband subsequently divorces and remarries her. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh, where the act of reconciliation through remarriage can substitute for the standard expiation of freeing a slave, fasting, or feeding the poor. It underscores the practical application of Quranic principles in marital law, ensuring that the ritual impurity of *Dhihar* is resolved through the restoration of the marital bond.
